questions.q: In the standard closing sequence, where does General Ledger close relative to the subledgers?
options: First, before any subledger closes
In the middle, between Payables and Receivables
Last, after Inventory, Payables/Purchasing, Receivables, Fixed Assets, and Cash Management
At the same time as every subledger, simultaneously
questions.explain: General Ledger closes last because it is where every subledger's activity ultimately lands and cannot be considered final until everything feeding it is.

questions.q: What does reconciling a subledger to GL actually confirm?
options: That the subledger's own balance matches its corresponding GL control account balance
That the chart of accounts has no inactive segments
That all journals used the Spot conversion rate
That the fiscal year calendar has 12 periods
questions.explain: Subledger-to-GL reconciliation confirms the subledger's balance (e.g., Payables) actually matches its GL control account, catching discrepancies posting alone wouldn't reveal.

questions.q: Why are key system accounts like Accounts Payable control or Intercompany accounts specifically reviewed during close?
options: Because they are never affected by any journal
Because they should normally only move through subledger or intercompany processes, so a stray ad hoc manual journal hitting them is a red flag
Because they only exist in foreign currency ledgers
Because they are deleted automatically at year-end
questions.explain: These control accounts are expected to move only through their normal process (e.g., subledger posting), so unexpected manual journal activity there needs investigation.

questions.q: Why is a successful journal posting not, by itself, proof that a period's books are correct?
options: Because posting only confirms debits equal credits mechanically; it doesn't confirm accounts were coded correctly or that subledgers actually reconcile to GL
Because posting always fails at least once per period
Because posting is unrelated to the trial balance
Because posting only applies to foreign currency journals
questions.explain: Successful posting only proves a journal met the debit-equals-credit mechanical requirement, not that everything downstream reconciles and is coded correctly.

questions.q: What is the final step of the General Ledger close checklist described in this lesson?
options: Running a currency revaluation
Changing the period's status from Open to Closed in Manage Accounting Period
Deleting all journals for the period
Creating the next fiscal year's calendar
questions.explain: After reconciliation, review, posting, and reporting are complete, the final step is changing the period status to Closed, covered fully in lesson 35.
